editorial:
Life with Father (1947) is a Technicolor comedy starring William Powell and Irene Dunne, with Elizabeth Taylor, Edmund Gwenn and ZaSu Pitts in the cast. The Internet Archive lists Warner Bros. as publisher. It adapts the 1939 stage play, which was inspired by Clarence Day's autobiography about his family in the 1880s.

The print may be free, but the dossier does not yet prove it. Text searches of the OCR of the 1974 and 1975 CCE renewal volumes for 'Life with Father' returned no entry. The search may not have covered the whole of either volume, because the fetch tool read only part of each file verbatim. The Copyright Office online catalog was not searched. The real trap is the source play. A separately renewed play would stay protected even if the film itself lapsed. Check the play's renewal before reuse. Internet Archive copies are uploader copies, and the uploader's Public Domain Mark is not a rights ruling.
faq: Is Life with Father (1947) public domain?

Not confirmed. Text searches of the OCR of the 1974 and 1975 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes for 'Life with Father' returned no renewal entry, but the search may not have covered the whole of either volume. The Copyright Office online catalog, the notice on the prints and the source play's status were not checked, so treat the film as unverified.
Can I reuse a copy from the Internet Archive?
Do not rely on the upload's Public Domain Mark. Confirm the film's renewal status and the status of the 1939 play it adapts first. Then use a clean source copy.
